title: A seven-hour call is really four hours ashore.
subtitle: Disembarkation, the coach queue, and an all-aboard set well before departure. Here is where it goes.

text: Take an hour off each end before you plan anything.
sub: The first hour ashore is queue. The last hour is all-aboard, which sits thirty to sixty minutes before departure. What remains is the day you actually have.

points.label: 08:00 — alongside
points.value: Do not join the first crush. Coffee on deck, and walk off at nine into an emptier town.

points.label: 09:00 — ashore
points.value: The two hours before the coach parties arrive are the only quiet ones you will get.

points.label: 12:00 — the one thing
points.value: One site, properly. Two sites is a coach tour with your name on it, not a day.

points.label: 13:30 — lunch inland
points.value: Ten minutes' walk from the waterfront halves the price and doubles the cooking.

points.label: 15:00 — turn around
points.value: Start back whatever you are mid-way through. The margin is the point of the plan.

points.label: 16:00 — all-aboard
points.value: Aboard with an hour spare, on deck, watching the lines come in. That is the reward.

title: Three thefts of a port day

items.head: Leaving with the first wave
items.body: Everyone tries to be first ashore, so nobody is. Twenty minutes' patience buys you a clear terminal.

items.head: Two sights in one call
items.body: The second one is always rushed, and the rushing is what you will remember of both.

items.head: Lunch on the harbour front
items.body: The most expensive and least interesting meal in any Mediterranean port is the one facing your ship.

text: In July, arrive early or arrive in October.
sub: Over-touristed calls are a scheduling problem before they are a crowd problem. Two ships alongside at ten means the old town belongs to you at nine, and to nobody at noon.

quote: A port day you remember has one thing in it and a long lunch. A port day you resent has four things and a coach.

title: Save this and use it on your next itinerary
body: Or tell me the sailing and I'll draft one port day properly — hours, the single thing worth doing, and where to eat away from the water.
